# Design: Adapter SDK

<!-- generated by @pingpong-solution — reference only -->

## Problem & Intent

Detect, Doctor, Launch, Scenario Driver, Collector, Static Provider, Source Mapper are separate capabilities (FR-024, CON-005). The core loads adapters via manifest + allowlist + version lock.

## Non-Goals

- Godot implementation
- Community adapter marketplace

## Assumptions

- Schema major version is 1.
- Fake adapter is sufficient for contract tests.
- Allowlist is local and static for MVP.

## Options Considered

### Option A: packages/adapter-sdk with manifest schema + harness (recommended)
- Summary: New package exports manifest schema, capability types, and contract test harness.
- Pros: Matches PRD layout; testable without core changes; clear boundary.
- Cons: New package.
- Evidence: PRD FR-024, CON-005.

### Option B: Manifest inside packages/core
- Summary: Core owns manifest validation.
- Pros: Fewer packages.
- Cons: Core becomes kitchen sink; adapters should not fork core.
- Evidence: Layer rules — adapters implement contracts, core loads them.

## Decision
**Chosen:** Option A

**Why:** Adapter contract is a first-class boundary (PRD §8). It needs its own tests and version lock.

## Cross-Domain Sign-Off
| Domain | Status | Note |
|--------|--------|------|
| KISS | ok | One schema + one harness fn |
| SOLID | ok | Adapters depend on contract, not core |
| DRY | ok | Capability enum is single source |
| Security | ok | Allowlist + version lock; no eval |
| UI/UX | n/a | No UI |
| Scaling | ok | Linear in adapters |
| Testability | ok | Fake adapter in tests |
| Maintainability | ok | Manifest schema is explicit |

## Confidence
**75%**

## Implementation Sketch

1. `packages/adapter-sdk/src/manifest.ts` — Zod schema for adapter manifest.
2. `packages/adapter-sdk/src/capabilities.ts` — capability types.
3. `packages/adapter-sdk/src/harness.ts` — contract test harness.
4. Tests: fake adapter passes; unknown capability rejected; schema major mismatch rejected.

## Open Questions

- Later: adapter loading mechanism in core.

YES
